static_traits.name: Xu Yulan
static_traits.educational_background: Currently studying for a bachelor's degree
static_traits.family_status: Living with a dog, without parents
static_traits.social_status: Has a few close friends to talk with, but has not yet discussed academic issues with them; relationship with professors and classmates strained by lateness
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no psychotherapy received before; no history of similar issues in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, better cooperation; tone on the negative and hesitant side; thinking relatively logical; tendencies toward catastrophizing, jumping to conclusions and overgeneralization are present

basic_info.main_problem: I am always late for class, which affects my academic performance and causes me a lot of stress.
basic_info.core_demands: Realizing that persistent lateness is affecting my academic future and causing significant stress, thus seeking counseling to address the lateness problem and reduce Academic pressure.

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am late again, it means I am irresponsible and unable to complete my studies
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Sets multiple alarms and reminders, rushes on the road
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am late again; I may never graduate.

special_situations.event: Lying in bed at night thinking about unfinished daytime matters, struggling to fall asleep
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not think through and resolve my worries, tomorrow will be worse and harder to get to class on time
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly thinking and worrying in bed; going to sleep late
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Many things were not done well today; tomorrow will be worse.

special_situations.event: When interacting with professors or classmates, receives negative feedback for lateness
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If they are dissatisfied with my lateness, it means I am an incompetent Student
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids discussing academic problems with friends to avoid being judged
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am unreliable and irresponsible.

special_situations.event: Feels tired and unmotivated when the morning alarm rings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I feel very tired, I am doomed to be unable to get to class on time
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Hitting snooze and staying in bed
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot get up; I will surely be late again today.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to control one's schedule, get to class on time and graduate smoothly, gaining others' recognition of oneself as a Student
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and negative evaluation, worrying about being seen as an irresponsible Student
defense_goal: Reducing Anxiety from trying by negating the effectiveness of plans and staying hesitant
Avoids discussing academic problems with friends to reduce the risk of criticism or embarrassment
Turning stress into self-rumination and insomnia to maintain a subjective sense of control over the problem

object_relations.self_representation: An incompetent Student who may be unable to graduate

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes new bedtime management techniques or step-by-step schedules
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing these methods are 'probably useless' for oneself, worrying about not persisting, thus negating the possibility of change
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gentle tone, first Empathizing with the concerns; avoiding direct confrontation with the negation, inviting attempts through micro-steps and small experiments; focusing on observable short-term goals with timely feedback on effectiveness.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When it involves discussing academic problems with others (friends) or the possibility of seeking support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worrying about being judged or looked down on, Anticipating negative interactions, thus choosing not to speak up
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using validating and supportive statements, inviting identification of self-critical statements and converting them into concrete requests; encouraging practicing help-seeking starting with low-risk people and small topics.

manifestations: Since the start of this semester, continually late, hard to self-direct and control one's schedule
Doubts whether he can graduate, feels low self-efficacy
Hesitating about and negating change plans, worrying about not persisting

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on
manifestations: Frequently questioning or negating the effectiveness of suggestions (e.g. 'I do not think it will help')
Emphasizing one's own Lack of motivation, worrying about not persisting, thus shrinking the space for attempts
Not yet discussing academic issues with friends, cautiously avoiding external support

positive_force: Willing to try and accept breaking tasks into small steps
Has a few close friends; has potential social support
Proposes feasible bedtime relaxation activities (breathing exercises, soothing music)
negative_force: Cognitive patterns of catastrophizing, jumping to conclusions, and overgeneralization
Fatigue from poor sleep quality and nighttime rumination
Avoids discussing academic problems with friends, reducing external support
Low Self-efficacy, doubt and negation toward change
Additional stress from Relationship tension with professors and classmates

antecedent: Disrupted sleep routine formed since this semester began
Exhaustion and lack of motivation when the morning alarm rings
Nighttime rumination leads to late nights and oversleeping
Anxiety intensified when realizing one will be late while heading out
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic and jumping-to-conclusions cognition about lateness and graduation ('lateness = unable to graduate'), triggering Anxiety and procrastination; insufficient sleep further reducing morning initiation.
target_behavior.function: Briefly escaping Demands and negative evaluation to reduce Anxiety (temporal negative Reinforcement)
target_behavior.consequence: Impaired Academic performance, Relationship tension with professors and classmates, escalating stress forming the vicious cycle of 'stress-insomnia-lateness'

target_behavior.behavior: Difficulty falling asleep at night and ruminative worries
antecedent: Thinking about unfinished daytime matters before sleep
Worrying about academic future and graduation possibility
Lacks an effective bedtime wind-down and relaxation routine
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing and jumping to conclusions maintain the worry; she tries to gain control through thinking but lacks effective boundaries and strategies.
target_behavior.function: Trying to gain subjective control and problem-solving through persistent thinking (an attempt at cognitive self-soothing), but actually maintaining Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Insufficient sleep, morning fatigue and low motivation, more likely to be late the next day
